note: Real-speech interrupt rates. For every silence run the watcher now reports, was the speaker followed by more speech? A 'no' at the file end is counted separately, not called a turn end.
conclusion: In recorded monologue, silence is essentially never a turn end: the speaker resumes ~100% of the time. The corpus is single-speaker continuous recordings, so the positive class (a speaker yielding the floor) is unrepresentable, not merely rare. Turn detection cannot be validated on this corpus.
